t: In 589 Sui troops entered Jiankang and the last Chen emperor surrendered, ending the Northern and Southern dynasties period and reuniting China proper.
The Sui built the Grand Canal, extended the Great Wall and rebuilt Luoyang as a planned capital, conscripting millions of workers at a heavy human cost.
Four expeditions against Goguryeo all failed by 614, and the dynasty disintegrated amid revolts that ended with Emperor Yang's assassination in 618.
dyk: The Sui army massed against Goguryeo was so large that the histories record it took 30 days for all its units to leave their rallying point near Shanhaiguan, and it stretched over about 410 kilometres.
ev: Yang Jian, regent for the child Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou, usurps the throne as Emperor Wen and names his dynasty Sui, after a bloody purge of 59 Zhou princes.
The Sui amass 518,000 troops along the northern bank of the Yangtze River, from Sichuan to the East China Sea, against the Chen dynasty.
Sui troops enter Jiankang and the last emperor of Chen surrenders; the city is razed and China proper is reunified.
Emperor Wen has relics of the Buddha distributed to temples throughout China, presenting himself as a Cakravartin king in imitation of Ashoka.
The Sui retake the Hanoi area from the Early Lý ruler Lý Phật Tử, opening the Linyi-Champa Campaign of 602–605.
Emperor Yang moves the capital to Luoyang, re-founded as a planned city, and enormously enlarges the Grand Canal works.
The last of four massive expeditions against Goguryeo ends in failure, leaving a deficit of money and men from which the Sui never recover.
Emperor Yang is assassinated by the minister Yuwen Huaji; in the north Li Yuan rises and takes the throne as Emperor Gaozu of Tang.

f.founder: Yang Jian, Emperor Wen of Sui
f.predecessor: Northern Zhou, whose throne Yang Jian usurped; the Chen dynasty in the south, conquered in 589
f.successor: Tang dynasty, founded by Li Yuan (Emperor Gaozu)
